prerequisites: Scientific and technical fundamentals acquired in basic engineering subjects
Basic principles of Thermodynamics, including the first and second principles
Mass and energy balances applied to physical systems
General fundamentals of Physics, especially in mechanics and energy
Basic algebra applied to solving equations
Mathematical analysis oriented to the formulation and resolution of engineering problems

learning_outcomes.text: Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize
Acquire the ability to effectively solve problems
Ability to apply knowledge to practice
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and lifelong learning
Knowledge of the basic principles of fluid mechanics
Understand the fundamental physical properties of fluids and their influence on the behavior of fluid-mechanical systems
Analyze phenomena related to fluid statics and dynamics, correctly interpreting the physical variables and characteristic magnitudes involved
Apply the fundamental laws of conservation of mass, energy, and momentum to solve engineering problems
Solve technical problems related to: hydrostatic forces, buoyancy, fluid transport, head losses, flow in closed conduits and open channels, hydraulic machinery, and compressible flow
Identify and adequately justify the physical hypotheses and simplifications necessary for the analysis of fluid systems
Critically interpret the obtained results, evaluating their physical consistency and applicability in real engineering contexts
Integrate the knowledge acquired in the subject with other industrial and energy-related subjects, promoting an applied and multidisciplinary vision of engineering

syllabus_topics: Introduction. Basic Considerations: Historical review of Fluid Mechanics. Units, Dimensions and Magnitudes. System of Units. Fundamental laws of Mechanics and Thermodynamics. Equations of State.

Properties of Fluids: Definition of fluid. Properties of fluids: density, specific weight, surface tension, vapor pressure, kinematic and dynamic viscosity, bulk modulus. Law of conservation of mass. Density, Specific weight, Relative density. Newton's law of viscosity. Newtonian fluids. Dynamic and Kinematic Viscosity. Properties of an ideal gas. Ideal gas law. Compressibility of fluids. Effect of pressure on the compressibility of gases in Isothermal and Isentropic processes.

Fluid Statics. Study of Pressure within a Fluid: Introduction. Concept of pressure. Units. Barometric and gauge pressure. Pressure at a point. Fundamental Law of Hydrostatics. Pascal's Principle. Energetic concept of piezometric heads. Pressure difference between two points. Incompressible fluids. Hydraulic press. Fluid column manometers. Compressible Fluids. Speed of sound. Mach number.

Study of Pressure Forces Exerted on Surfaces: Introduction. Study of pressure forces exerted on submerged flat surfaces. Study of pressure forces exerted on curved surfaces. Gravity dams. Buoyant forces on submerged bodies. Archimedes' Principle. Stability of submerged bodies. Stability of floating bodies. Center of Gravity and Metacentric Height.

Fluid Dynamics. Fundamentals of Fluid Motion: Translation motion of liquid masses. Constant linear acceleration. Rotation motion in open and closed containers. Description of fluid motion. Lagrangian and Eulerian description of motion. Definitions: Trajectory, streamlines and stream tube. Flow rate or Volumetric flow, Mass flow. Classification of Flows: One-dimensional Flow, Reynolds Transport Theorem. Continuity Equation.

Momentum Law, Newton's 2nd Principle Applied to Fluid Flow: Introduction. Newton's Laws. Control Volume. Force exchanged with the fluid, due to a variation in the momentum of the flow. Momentum Law. Applications: Force exerted on the surface of a blade. Force exerted by the flow in a Nozzle. Force exerted by the flow when passing through a gate. Principle of operation of Turbomachines. Moment of Momentum.

Bernoulli's Equation. Ideal Transport Conditions: Bernoulli's Equation. Energetic concept of Bernoulli's equation terms. Total pressure. Static pressure. Dynamic pressure, Piezometer, Pitot tube. Energy grade line and hydraulic grade line. Applications of Bernoulli's equation, Restrictions in its use: Torricelli's Theorem. Venturi effect. Velocity calculation. Analysis of head terms in a Siphon. Formulation of Bernoulli's equation, in cases of unsteady flow, compressible flow, isothermal flow and adiabatic flow.

General Energy Equation: First law of Thermodynamics. Energy conservation. Extension of Bernoulli's Equation, with mechanical energy exchange terms. Energy treatment for Centrifugal pumps. Net head. Energy treatment for Turbines. Net head. Head loss term in fluid transport. Flow rate measurement.

Fluid Transport in Closed Conduits: Reynolds experiment. Laminar and Turbulent flow regime. Reynolds Number. Calculation of head losses in Laminar regime. Hagen-Poiseuille Equation. Darcy-Weisbach Equation. Friction coefficient. Calculation of head losses in Turbulent regime. Colebrook Equation. Moody Diagram. Calculation of flow in simple pipes. Minor losses: Loss coefficients and Equivalent lengths. Non-circular sections. Hydraulic Radius. Characteristic Curve of a Pipe. Simple Piping Systems. Branched pipes. Calculation of Pipe Networks. Generalized network equation. Hardy-Cross method. Numerical methods.

Compressible Flow: Stagnation properties. Speed of sound and Mach number. One-dimensional Isentropic Flow. Isentropic flow in nozzles. Shock waves. Flow in ducts with energy transfer. Adiabatic flow in ducts with friction.

Fluid Transport in Open Channels: Introduction. Classification of open channel flow. Uniform flow. Normal depth. Subcritical, Critical and Supercritical flow regime. Energetic analysis of open channel flow. Uniform flow without friction. Flow with friction. Uniform flow with friction. Hydraulic jump. Flow control and measurement. Gate and Weirs. Optimal cross-sections in rectangular, trapezoidal and circular channels.

Dimensional Analysis and Hydraulic Machinery: Experimentation in fluid mechanics. Dimensional analysis. Buckingham Pi Theorem. Common dimensionless parameters. Laws of similarity. Generalities on hydraulic pumps. Characteristic curves. Efficiencies. Generalities on hydraulic turbines. Efficiencies.
teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (exposition of principles, doubt resolution, case analysis, guided exercises, flipped learning)

Practical classes (problem solving, modeling and simulation with EES software, individual and teamwork on technical exercises, analysis of fluid-mechanical installations, validation of engineering models)
Integrative project (team-based analysis and simulation of a fluid-mechanical system)
Autonomous student work (study, exercises, project development, technical reports, review, evaluation preparation, critical use of digital tools)
Tutorials and academic monitoring (individual and group tutorials for doubts, guidance, project follow-up, feedback)
assessment_rules: Problem-solving and practical cases tests, as well as knowledge tests, require a minimum grade of 5 out of 10 to pass. The continuous assessment questionnaires and the integrative project do not have a specific minimum grade. The integrative project grade is not recoverable in the second call. If a student achieves an overall grade of 5.0 or higher but does not meet one of the minimums, the final grade will be 4.9. In the second call, students only need to retake the failed components, and grade improvement is not allowed for those who passed in the first call.
